bedrock.name: Amazon Bedrock
bedrock.role: Managed foundation-model APIs, supported customization/import, and GenAI application features.
bedrock.boundary: Choose from supported model contracts; instance and GPU selection are abstracted.
details: Invoke compatible models through Converse or their native model API.
Add supported Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, prompt management, and evaluation capabilities.
Select model access, delivery, and capacity separately from application hosting.
bedrock.useWhen: A supported foundation model and managed GenAI features fit your application.

sagemaker.name: SageMaker AI
sagemaker.role: Managed ML lifecycle and hosting with chosen containers, instances, and endpoint scaling.
sagemaker.boundary: Owning serving configuration also means sizing and operating its capacity.
details: Prepare data, run training/tuning jobs, and register versioned model packages.
Choose real-time, asynchronous, batch, or CPU-only serverless inference; Serverless Provisioned Concurrency still has no GPU.
Configure serving resources, scaling, deployment verification, and monitoring.
sagemaker.useWhen: You need control over the model artifact, serving container, GPU, or endpoint scaling.

neo.name: SageMaker Neo
neo.role: Compile supported models for a specified edge or cloud hardware target.
neo.boundary: Check model/operator and target support; compilation is different from providing edge infrastructure.
details: Compile a supported trained model for a specified hardware/software target.
Check operator, framework, and target compatibility before choosing the path.
Deploy the compiled artifact through a compatible runtime; compilation does not host it.
neo.useWhen: A supported model must be optimized for a specific deployment target.

hybrid.name: Outposts / Wavelength
hybrid.role: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure on premises; Wavelength places compute in supported carrier networks.
hybrid.boundary: Verify service availability and data paths; these products do not automatically keep every dependency local.
details: Outposts places supported AWS infrastructure in your premises.
Wavelength places supported compute in carrier networks for mobile edge workloads.
Check where inference, data, identity, and every remote dependency actually run.
hybrid.useWhen: Infrastructure location or mobile-network latency is a hard requirement.

registry.name: Model Registry
registry.role: Version model packages, evaluation evidence, and approval status.
registry.boundary: Approval does not update a live endpoint or load an adapter.
details: Group related model packages and record a version for each candidate.
Attach evaluation evidence, artifact references, and approval status.
A separate release process creates or updates serving resources from the approved package.
registry.useWhen: A candidate model needs traceable versions and an explicit approval decision.

appconfig.name: AWS AppConfig
appconfig.role: Deploy validated runtime configuration and feature variants with controlled rollout.
appconfig.boundary: The application must fetch and apply changes; propagation follows deployment and polling.
details: Organize configuration profiles and deployment environments under an application.
Validate configuration and apply a deployment strategy with configured monitoring.
The application retrieves and applies the deployed version through an agent or API.
appconfig.useWhen: Model mappings, prompts, or feature flags must change through a controlled rollout.

paramstore.name: Parameter Store
paramstore.role: Store configuration values, including KMS-protected SecureString parameters.
paramstore.boundary: Use AppConfig for staged rollout and Secrets Manager for managed secret rotation.
details: Store named strings, string lists, or KMS-protected SecureString values.
Use parameter paths and IAM policies to separate environments and applications.
Read and apply the value in application code; storing it does not perform a rollout.
paramstore.useWhen: The application needs centrally stored configuration values with scoped access.

cicd.name: CodePipeline / CodeBuild
cicd.role: Automate builds, assertions, evaluation gates, release, and rollback.
cicd.boundary: Define pass/fail criteria and approval explicitly; a completed job is not a quality decision.
details: Build code and infrastructure from versioned source and artifacts.
Run schema/business assertions and held-out quality checks against a baseline.
Promote, verify, or roll back the actual prompt/model/configuration version.
cicd.useWhen: Changes must pass repeatable checks before reaching the production route.

s3.name: Amazon S3
s3.role: Keep versioned source documents, evaluation sets, artifacts, and batch input/output.
s3.boundary: Source updates need downstream synchronization; object permissions do not authorize indexed copies.
details: Store source documents, training/evaluation datasets, and generated job outputs.
Track the bucket, key, and source version in downstream chunk metadata.
Connect source events to a controlled synchronization pipeline.
s3.useWhen: You need durable source files, versioned evidence, or batch artifacts.

glue.name: AWS Glue
glue.role: Prepare datasets, catalog schemas, and evaluate Data Quality rules before ingestion or training.
glue.boundary: Configure failure/quarantine and preserve source versions; a catalog is not a retrieval index.
details: Crawlers and the Data Catalog describe supported source schemas and locations.
ETL jobs clean, transform, and write approved datasets.
Data Quality rules produce results; configure failure, quarantine, or remediation explicitly.
glue.useWhen: Data needs preparation, cataloging, and quality gates before ingestion or training.

datawrangler.name: Data Wrangler / Processing
datawrangler.role: Visual preparation in Data Wrangler; custom batch scripts in SageMaker Processing.
datawrangler.boundary: Choose according to the required transformation and existing pipeline.
details: Data Wrangler supports visual preparation and data insights.
Processing runs your scripts for preprocessing, evaluation, or batch transformations.
Record input/output artifacts so a pipeline can reproduce the preparation step.
datawrangler.useWhen: Visual data preparation or custom SageMaker batch preprocessing fits the workflow.

textract.name: Amazon Textract
textract.role: Extract supported document text, forms, tables, queries, invoices, and ID fields.
textract.boundary: Select the analysis API; OCR alone does not reconstruct all document relationships.
details: DetectDocumentText returns OCR text; AnalyzeDocument adds selected document features.
FORMS, TABLES, and QUERIES solve different extraction needs.
Use supported expense/ID APIs or asynchronous document operations where appropriate.
textract.useWhen: You need document structure such as forms, tables, or answers from supported files.

bda.name: Bedrock Data Automation
bda.role: Convert supported documents and media into standard output or blueprint-defined fields.
bda.boundary: Validate fields before downstream writes; extraction does not create embeddings or orchestrate the application.
details: Standard output provides supported document or media representations.
Custom blueprints define business fields inside the invoked project.
Configure input/output permissions and validate results before database or index writes.
bda.useWhen: Supported document/media input must become managed structured extraction output.

transcribe.name: Amazon Transcribe
transcribe.role: Convert supported speech to text with batch or streaming workflows.
transcribe.boundary: Preserve turns; speaker labels identify speakers, not verified business roles.
details: Choose supported batch transcription or a streaming speech workflow.
Use diarization for mixed speakers; channel identification for separately recorded channels.
Preserve speaker turns and timestamps; verify any mapping to customer, doctor, or employee roles.
transcribe.useWhen: Speech must become searchable text or input to a voice application.

comprehend.name: Amazon Comprehend
comprehend.role: Analyze text entities, key phrases, sentiment, classification, and supported PII spans.
comprehend.boundary: Detection returns evidence; your pipeline must apply redaction where required.
details: DetectSentiment labels the whole text; targeted sentiment examines entity mentions.
Entity/key-phrase detection extracts spans rather than producing a summary.
Custom classification categorizes documents; custom recognition identifies domain-specific entities.
comprehend.useWhen: Text needs entity, sentiment, classification, or supported sensitive-span analysis.

medical.name: Comprehend Medical
medical.role: Extract clinical entities and supported PHI from medical text.
medical.boundary: Verify entity coverage, offsets, and confidence before redacting or retaining audit data.
details: Choose the supported clinical-entity or PHI operation for the task.
Apply offsets to the exact analyzed text; preserve encoding and text alignment.
Use confidence and coverage checks before redaction, indexing, or clinical downstream use.
medical.useWhen: Clinical text needs supported medical entities or PHI span detection.

rekognition.name: Amazon Rekognition
rekognition.role: Analyze images and supported video for labels, moderation, faces, and other visual features.
rekognition.boundary: Use document extraction for forms/tables; availability varies by feature.
details: Analyze supported labels, moderation categories, faces, and other visual features.
Select the image API or supported asynchronous video workflow.
Face detection locates a face; identity matching requires a separate supported setup.
rekognition.useWhen: Supported images or video need visual analysis or moderation.

kb.name: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
kb.role: Coordinate supported ingestion, embeddings, retrieval, and retrieval-plus-generation.
kb.boundary: Configure sync and trusted access filters; the backing store and connector limit available features.
details: Configure a data source, parser, chunking strategy, embedding model, and supported store.
Run and inspect ingestion jobs to keep indexed evidence current.
Retrieve returns candidates; the combined generation API depends on the Knowledge Base type.
kb.useWhen: You want a supported RAG pipeline inside an application you control.

embeddings.name: Bedrock embedding models
embeddings.role: Encode compatible corpus and query inputs as vectors.
embeddings.boundary: Changing the embedding model requires a compatible rebuilt corpus index; equal dimensions are insufficient.
details: Encode source chunks during ingestion and queries during retrieval.
Match the model, dimensions, and preprocessing across corpus and query paths.
Measure retrieval quality before reducing dimensions or switching models.
embeddings.useWhen: Documents and questions need a compatible vector representation for search.

opensearch.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
opensearch.role: Provide lexical, vector, and hybrid search with index and ranking controls.
opensearch.boundary: Benchmark recall, filters, latency, and idle capacity; vector count alone does not decide the platform.
details: Define mappings and index supported text/vector fields.
Tune HNSW search/build effort and measure recall, memory, and latency.
For Serverless, check IAM, data-access, and network policies together.
opensearch.useWhen: Your search requirements need lexical, vector, hybrid, or ranking controls.

aurora.name: Aurora / RDS pgvector
aurora.role: Keep supported vector indexes alongside PostgreSQL records and SQL queries.
aurora.boundary: Transactions and relational integration can matter more than a blanket scale cutoff.
details: Use pgvector types and supported indexes in PostgreSQL.
Combine relational predicates with the required similarity query.
Benchmark filtering, index behavior, concurrency, and operational cost on your workload.
aurora.useWhen: Vector similarity belongs alongside PostgreSQL records, joins, or transactions.

s3vectors.name: Amazon S3 Vectors
s3vectors.role: Store and query vectors in dedicated S3 vector buckets and indexes.
s3vectors.boundary: Check filterable metadata, connector/search support, and latency requirements; vector buckets differ from ordinary S3 buckets.
details: Create a vector bucket and an index with a compatible dimension and distance metric.
Write vectors with keys and supported metadata, then query using a compatible vector.
Choose filterable metadata deliberately and check connector-specific support.
s3vectors.useWhen: Dedicated vector storage/query economics fit the required search contract.

neptune.name: Neptune Analytics / GraphRAG
neptune.role: Retrieve using relationships between linked entities and supporting evidence.
neptune.boundary: Use a measured multi-hop need; managed GraphRAG has its own chunking and graph-build contract.
details: Represent linked entities and supporting evidence through a supported graph workflow.
Use graph relationships to complement similarity-based retrieval.
Check the managed GraphRAG graph-build and chunking contract before customization.
neptune.useWhen: Relationships and multi-hop evidence matter to the question.

kendra.name: Amazon Kendra
kendra.role: Enterprise search/retrieval with supported connectors and document ACLs.
kendra.boundary: Maintenance mode: assess existing-customer eligibility and migration requirements.
details: Connect supported enterprise sources and synchronize content plus document ACLs.
Query or retrieve using the configured identity and access context.
Use search analytics and explicit feedback to investigate relevance gaps.
kendra.useWhen: An existing eligible enterprise-search deployment needs retrieval and connector integration.

availability.text: Closed to new customers; assess Knowledge Bases for a new application.

reranking.name: Bedrock reranking
reranking.role: Rescore retrieved candidates so context selection can favor relevant evidence.
reranking.boundary: Cannot recover a missing candidate; measure evidence retention after pruning.
details: Submit a query and candidate sources to a supported reranking model.
Use relevance scores to select a measured context set.
Compare relevance and evidence loss before choosing a cutoff or result count.
reranking.useWhen: Relevant evidence is retrieved but context selection needs better ordering.

apigw.name: Amazon API Gateway
apigw.role: Expose supported REST, HTTP, or WebSocket integrations with authentication and request controls.
apigw.boundary: API keys and request throttles do not supply user authorization or a hard token-spend cap.
details: Choose REST, HTTP, or WebSocket according to the integration and client contract.
Configure authentication, validation, throttling, and observability for the entry point.
Supported REST proxy response streaming differs from WebSocket callbacks and HTTP APIs.
apigw.useWhen: Clients need a managed API entry point with an appropriate transport and authorizer.

appsync.name: AWS AppSync
appsync.role: Provide GraphQL APIs and supported real-time subscription/event delivery.
appsync.boundary: Choose for the client interaction contract; still enforce record-level permissions.
details: Define the GraphQL schema and map resolvers to supported data sources.
Use subscriptions for supported updates tied to the configured API contract.
Derive record scope from trusted identity and enforce it at the resolver/backend.
appsync.useWhen: The client contract calls for GraphQL queries, mutations, or subscriptions.

promptmgmt.name: Bedrock Prompt Management
promptmgmt.role: Store reusable templates, variables, model settings, variants, and immutable versions.
promptmgmt.boundary: Versioning does not test, approve, or promote a prompt by itself.
details: Define supported prompt variants, variables, and inference configuration.
Create an immutable version and invoke the intended version ARN.
Capture the rendered request and compare candidates before promoting the live route.
promptmgmt.useWhen: Templates and model settings need reusable, auditable prompt versions.

promptopt.name: Bedrock Prompt Optimization
promptopt.role: Generate prompt revisions tailored to a supported target model.
promptopt.boundary: Evaluate quality and token cost; optimization does not change weights or retrieve facts.
details: Supply a supported prompt and target model to the optimization workflow.
Evaluate the proposed revision against the unchanged baseline.
Measure output quality and token cost; a longer revision can cost more.
promptopt.useWhen: A supported model may respond better to revised instructions or wording.

converse.name: Converse / ConverseStream
converse.role: Use a common message interface across compatible models; stream supported responses.
converse.boundary: Model capabilities still vary; supply required conversation history on each call.
details: Send user/assistant content in messages and common settings in inferenceConfig.
Read the returned message, usage, and stopReason.
ConverseStream emits events; the application must consume and forward them incrementally.
converse.useWhen: You want to compare compatible models while keeping one application message contract.

invokemodel.name: InvokeModel / streaming
invokemodel.role: Invoke a model using its native request and response contract.
invokemodel.boundary: The client path must also forward stream events incrementally.
details: Serialize the provider-specific request and decode its native response.
Parameter names and output fields depend on the selected model contract.
Use InvokeModelWithResponseStream when that model supports native streaming.
invokemodel.useWhen: You need a supported model-native request body or model-specific capability.

params.name: Inference parameters
params.role: Control supported sampling, output length, and stop conditions.
params.boundary: A low temperature or valid JSON does not establish factual correctness.
details: Temperature and supported top-p/top-k settings affect sampling.
maxTokens limits output; inspect stopReason when an answer truncates.
Use supported stop sequences and task-based evaluation rather than universal presets.
params.useWhen: Output length, variability, or stopping behavior needs controlled adjustment.

dynamodb.name: Amazon DynamoDB
dynamodb.role: Persist scoped sessions, job status, ratings, and conditional idempotency records.
dynamodb.boundary: TTL deletion is asynchronous; conditional writes must be part of a complete action/reconciliation design.
details: Choose partition/sort keys that express tenant, session, or action identity.
Use conditional writes for state transitions and duplicate-work protection.
Track logical expiry and reconcile external side effects after retries or partial failures.
dynamodb.useWhen: The application needs scoped session state, job status, or idempotency records.

lex.name: Amazon Lex
lex.role: Build intent/slot-driven text and voice conversations with backend fulfillment.
lex.boundary: Choose the conversation contract deliberately; open-ended tool planning requires a different controller.
details: Define intents and slots for the supported text/voice interaction.
Collect required information before invoking backend fulfillment.
Validate and authorize the business action outside the conversational response.
lex.useWhen: The conversation follows known intents, required slots, and fulfillment rules.

polly.name: Amazon Polly
polly.role: Synthesize speech from text using supported voices and delivery modes.
polly.boundary: Measure the whole voice pipeline; a streaming hop does not guarantee an end-to-end latency target.
details: Select an engine, voice, language, and output format that work together.
Supply plain text or supported SSML for speech synthesis.
Measure buffering and playback alongside upstream transcription and generation.
polly.useWhen: Text must become speech in a supported voice and audio format.

routing.name: Intelligent Prompt Routing
routing.role: Route each request between a supported pair of models according to predicted quality.
routing.boundary: Managed routing support is model-family specific; custom cascading needs your own escalation policy.
details: Invoke the supported prompt router through its modelId/ARN.
The managed router selects between its configured model options.
A custom easy-first cascade requires application calls and an evaluated escalation rule.
routing.useWhen: A supported managed model pair can handle mixed request difficulty.

caching.name: Prompt / response caching
caching.role: Reuse a shared prefix with Bedrock prompt caching; reuse answers through an application cache.
caching.boundary: Answer caches require entitlement, version, policy, and freshness checks; semantic matches can be wrong.
details: Prompt caching marks supported stable prefixes; inference still generates the answer.
Exact/semantic answer caches are application-managed and reuse finished responses.
Revalidate authorization, source versions, model/prompt policy, and expiry on cache hits.
caching.useWhen: Repeated prefix processing or safely reusable answers dominate request cost.

cloudfront.name: Amazon CloudFront
cloudfront.role: Cache eligible shared content near clients and protect supported origins.
cloudfront.boundary: Personalized or permission-sensitive answers need correct cache keys and access policy.
details: Configure an origin, cache policy, TTLs, and any required origin access controls.
Include all response-varying values in the caching design.
Invalidate or version stale content; avoid cross-user reuse of private answers.
cloudfront.useWhen: Eligible shared content can be cached near users.

provthroughput.name: Provisioned Throughput
provthroughput.role: Reserve eligible model capacity when measured sustained use justifies it.
provthroughput.boundary: Invoke the provisioned resource and account for idle/commitment charges; capacity is not an end-to-end latency guarantee.
details: Select an eligible model, model-unit capacity, and commitment contract.
Invoke the provisioned resource ARN rather than an unrelated on-demand model ID.
Monitor utilization, throttling, and idle cost independently of application compute.
provthroughput.useWhen: Measured sustained use justifies supported reserved model capacity.

xregion.name: Cross-Region inference
xregion.role: Use a supported inference profile to route eligible model requests across its destination Regions.
xregion.boundary: Validate every destination; model routing does not fail over your application.
details: Pass the inference profile ID/ARN as modelId.
Approve the source/destination permissions and applicable organizational policies.
Check geographic/global scope separately from application disaster recovery.
xregion.useWhen: Eligible inference may use every destination in an approved profile.

agentcore.name: Bedrock AgentCore
agentcore.role: Host custom agents or use a managed harness with modular memory, tools, identity, and observability.
agentcore.boundary: The chosen controller owns planning; business APIs still enforce authority.
details: Runtime hosts compatible code; a managed harness can own supported agent execution.
Gateway connects supported tools; Identity brokers configured credentials.
Add scoped memory, policy, and telemetry according to the workload.
agentcore.useWhen: An agent needs supported hosting, tool connectivity, identity, or managed execution components.

agentidentity.name: AgentCore Identity
agentidentity.role: Support agent identity and authorized access to supported downstream credentials.
agentidentity.boundary: Runtime/Gateway inbound authentication and outbound credential brokerage are configured separately. Target business rules still apply.
details: Configure Runtime/Gateway inbound trust separately from outbound credential access.
Associate supported credential providers and permissions with the intended agent workflow.
Keep user consent, credential scope, and target application authorization explicit.
agentidentity.useWhen: An agent needs configured inbound identity or delegated access to downstream services.

mcp.name: MCP tool integration
mcp.role: Standardize tool discovery and calls through a supported MCP client/server transport.
mcp.boundary: MCP is a protocol; hosting, user identity, and action permissions remain design decisions.
details: A client discovers available tool names, input schemas, and descriptions.
Calls exchange structured arguments and results over a supported transport.
Choose hosting, identity validation, and per-tool authority independently of the protocol.
mcp.useWhen: Agents need a common contract to discover and call tools.

multiagent.name: Strands / Agent Squad
multiagent.role: Implement custom agent collaboration or specialist request routing.
multiagent.boundary: Use the required coordination pattern; multiple agents add handoff and evaluation work.
details: Use Strands for a custom agent implementation and supported collaboration patterns.
Use Agent Squad where specialist routing/orchestration fits the application.
Define handoff contracts, scoped context, termination, and end-to-end task evaluation.
multiagent.useWhen: Specialist routing or collaboration improves a measured task enough to justify coordination.

agents.name: Bedrock Agents Classic
agents.role: Run existing managed agents with instructions, action groups, knowledge bases, and traces.
agents.boundary: Closed to new customers; AWS directs new implementations toward AgentCore.
details: Configure instructions, action groups, and Knowledge Base integrations.
Promote versions/aliases and invoke the intended agent alias.
Enable supported traces to inspect tool calls, observations, and orchestration events.
agents.useWhen: You maintain an existing eligible Bedrock Agents Classic application.

availability.text: Agents Classic is closed to new customers; check AgentCore migration guidance.

stepfns.name: AWS Step Functions
stepfns.role: Persist explicit workflow states, branching, retries, and supported service integrations.
stepfns.boundary: Choose Standard for long approvals or callback task tokens; Express has a different duration/integration contract.
details: Use Choice for branching, Map for a collection, and Parallel for independent branches.
Standard supports long workflows and supported callback task-token integrations.
Express supports short workflows and Wait states, with no .sync or callback task tokens.
stepfns.useWhen: The business process has explicit states, retries, or durable approval waits.

flows.name: Bedrock Flows
flows.role: Build versioned visual GenAI pipelines using supported nodes and conditions.
flows.boundary: Use a durable workflow for broader business state and long approval waits.
details: Connect prompt/model, retrieval, condition, and supported integration nodes.
Wire both the original input and intermediate results to downstream consumers.
Version the flow and invoke its intended alias; evaluate malformed/unknown branches.
flows.useWhen: A visual GenAI pipeline fits the supported node and branching contract.

lambda.name: AWS Lambda
lambda.role: Run bounded handlers, tool adapters, validation, and ingestion transformations.
lambda.boundary: Reserved concurrency caps concurrency; provisioned concurrency initializes environments. Neither reserves model capacity.
details: Run application code without maintaining a long-lived server.
Reserved concurrency allocates/caps concurrent execution; provisioned concurrency initializes environments.
Externalize durable job state and make retried side effects safe.
lambda.useWhen: A bounded event handler, validator, or tool adapter fits the execution contract.

events.name: EventBridge / S3 events
events.role: Route matching events or schedules to supported targets.
events.boundary: Check source-to-target integration support; routing does not perform the target work.
details: Enable the source and define event-pattern or schedule matching.
S3 direct notifications and EventBridge rules have different destination contracts.
Configure target permissions, failure handling, and downstream idempotency.
events.useWhen: Events need filtering, fan-out, scheduling, or delivery to a supported target.

sqs.name: Amazon SQS / SNS
sqs.role: SQS retains work for consumers; SNS fans notifications out to subscribers.
sqs.boundary: Configure pacing, retries, dead-letter handling, and idempotency; a queue alone is not a token-rate limiter.
details: SQS buffers work until consumers process and acknowledge it.
SNS fans notifications out to supported subscriptions, including queues.
Tune consumer pacing, visibility timeout, retries, DLQ, and duplicate handling.
sqs.useWhen: Work must survive bursts or one event must reach several subscribers.

cognito.name: Amazon Cognito
cognito.role: User pools authenticate application users and issue tokens; identity pools exchange supported identities for temporary AWS credentials.
cognito.boundary: User-pool JWTs and temporary IAM-role credentials are different artifacts. Application resource authorization still applies.
details: User pools authenticate users directly or through supported external identity providers.
Validate issuer, audience/client, expiry, signature, and the required token type.
Add an identity pool only when the supported client needs temporary AWS credentials.
cognito.useWhen: Customers or application users need sign-in, federation, and tokens for your application.

idc.name: IAM Identity Center
idc.role: Provide workforce federation, account access, and permission sets.
idc.boundary: Permission sets configure account-role policies; document ACLs and business entitlements need their own mapping.
details: Federate a corporate identity provider or use a supported identity source.
Assign users/groups to accounts and permission sets.
Account access creates an assigned IAM role session with temporary AWS credentials.
idc.useWhen: Employees need centrally assigned access to AWS accounts or supported applications.

iam.name: AWS IAM / Organizations SCPs
iam.role: IAM grants scoped AWS permissions; applicable SCPs constrain the account permission ceiling.
iam.boundary: An SCP never grants access; neither control replaces business record authorization.
details: Identity/resource policies participate in the applicable AWS permission evaluation.
Role trust determines who may assume a role; permission policies determine its allowed actions.
Permissions boundaries, session policies, and applicable SCPs restrict available permissions.
iam.useWhen: A principal needs permission to call an AWS action on a resource.

vpce.name: VPC endpoints / PrivateLink
vpce.role: Reach supported AWS APIs over private interface endpoints.
vpce.boundary: Private routing needs the correct service endpoint, DNS, network access, and IAM policy.
details: Select the correct interface service, such as bedrock-runtime for model inference.
Configure ENIs, DNS, HTTPS reachability, and endpoint policy.
Use identity/resource permissions as well; private connectivity is not an access grant.
vpce.useWhen: Supported AWS API traffic needs an explicitly controlled private network path.

kms.name: KMS / Secrets Manager
kms.role: Manage encryption keys and protected credentials with supported rotation.
kms.boundary: Key policy, decryption rights, and secret use are separate from user entitlement.
details: KMS manages encryption keys, key policies, and supported cryptographic operations.
Secrets Manager stores protected credentials and supports configured rotation.
Grant only the key/secret operations the workload needs and avoid raw values in logs.
kms.useWhen: You need controlled encryption-key use or managed protected credentials.

lakeformation.name: AWS Lake Formation
lakeformation.role: Apply supported fine-grained lake permissions through integrated query engines.
lakeformation.boundary: Independent direct S3 access can bypass those filters; remove bypass paths.
details: Register supported lake locations and define the intended grants/data filters.
Query through an integrated engine using the authorized identity.
Remove independent source access that would bypass the lake permission path.
lakeformation.useWhen: Supported lake query engines need table, column, or row-level data permissions.

s3gov.name: S3 Object Lock / Lifecycle
s3gov.role: Apply supported immutable retention/legal hold and age-based transition or expiry.
s3gov.boundary: WORM retention and routine expiry solve different requirements; coordinate derived copies and legal holds.
details: Object Lock supplies supported WORM retention and legal-hold controls.
Lifecycle rules transition or expire eligible objects/versions according to age.
Coordinate retention across sources, derived indexes, caches, backups, and audit records.
s3gov.useWhen: Stored objects need immutable retention/legal hold or age-based lifecycle management.

waf.name: AWS WAF
waf.role: Filter supported HTTP requests for abuse, bots, and common web attacks.
waf.boundary: Check entry-point integration; web filtering does not establish semantic prompt safety.
details: Attach a web ACL to a supported protected resource.
Evaluate configured managed/custom rules and supported rate-based controls.
Investigate sampled requests and metrics without treating web filtering as model authorization.
waf.useWhen: A supported HTTP entry point needs web-request filtering or abuse controls.

macie.name: Amazon Macie
macie.role: Discover supported sensitive data in eligible ordinary S3 objects and report findings.
macie.boundary: Findings do not redact content; review skipped objects and unsupported vector buckets.
details: Use automated discovery or configured classification jobs for supported coverage.
Review findings plus skipped, unsupported, or failed objects.
Send confirmed issues to a separate remediation/redaction workflow.
macie.useWhen: Eligible ordinary S3 objects need sensitive-data discovery and classification.

guardrails.name: Bedrock Guardrails
guardrails.role: Apply supported content, topic, word, PII, grounding, and reasoning policies.
guardrails.boundary: Verify coverage at each input/output stage; prompt-attack checks do not assess toolResult content.
details: Select content, topic, word, sensitive-information, grounding, or reasoning policies as supported.
Attach the intended guardrail version to inference or call ApplyGuardrail separately.
Consume the returned action, assessments, and permitted/sanitized content in application code.
guardrails.useWhen: Supported model-content risks need configured checks at input/output boundaries.

evaluations.name: Bedrock Evaluations
evaluations.role: Evaluate supported model or RAG outputs using automated, judge, or human methods.
evaluations.boundary: Choose the metric and reference data for the failed quality; define release thresholds outside job completion.
details: Choose programmatic metrics, an LLM judge, or human review for the target behavior.
Keep prompts, references, rubrics, and critical cohorts versioned and comparable.
Inspect the report and enforce promotion thresholds outside job completion.
evaluations.useWhen: A model, prompt, or RAG change needs measured quality evidence.

human.name: Ground Truth / A2I
human.role: Create training labels or route selected predictions to human review.
human.boundary: Existing-customer availability applies; model-comparison evaluation is a separate workflow.
details: Ground Truth creates labels for supported training tasks.
A2I routes selected supported predictions into a configured human loop.
Define the workforce, work team, instructions, and downstream handling of reviewed results.
human.useWhen: An existing eligible workflow needs training labels or human prediction review.

availability.text: Ground Truth/A2I have existing-customer restrictions; check workforce and service availability.

clarify.name: Clarify / Model Monitor
clarify.role: Analyze bias/explanations and run supported production data/model drift checks.
clarify.boundary: Existing-customer availability applies; drift is a signal to investigate, not proof of lower task accuracy.
details: Clarify analyzes configured bias metrics and feature-attribution explanations.
Model Monitor compares supported captured data/results with configured baselines.
Model-quality checks need ground truth; investigate drift against actual task performance.
clarify.useWhen: An existing eligible deployment needs supported bias, explanation, or monitoring workflows.

availability.text: Clarify and Model Monitor are closed to new customers.

modelcard.name: Model Cards / Dashboard
modelcard.role: Document model use, limitations, and evidence; inspect governance and monitoring coverage.
modelcard.boundary: Documentation and a dashboard do not automatically configure quality checks.
details: Document intended use, training/evaluation information, limitations, and risks.
Record the model version and evidence used for the release decision.
Use the dashboard to inspect governance/monitoring status, then configure missing controls.
modelcard.useWhen: Reviewers need model purpose, limitations, evidence, and monitoring coverage in one place.

cloudwatch.name: Amazon CloudWatch
cloudwatch.role: Collect metrics/logs and alert on operational trends such as tokens, latency, and errors.
cloudwatch.boundary: Aggregate health does not explain answer quality or every slow dependency.
details: Inspect requests, token counts, latency, throttles, and failures with appropriate dimensions.
Use Logs Insights to investigate enabled structured application/invocation logs.
Attach actionable alarms and correlate service metrics with request/version identifiers.
cloudwatch.useWhen: You need runtime metrics, logs, dashboards, and operational alarms.

synthetics.name: CloudWatch Synthetics
synthetics.role: Replay configured user journeys to detect availability and latency failures.
synthetics.boundary: Pair workflow checks with representative answer and tool-outcome evaluation.
details: Run a configured canary against the required application path.
Assert expected behavior and retain evidence of failures.
Use separate representative evaluations for answer quality beyond that journey.
synthetics.useWhen: A repeatable user journey should be checked for availability and latency.

cost.name: AWS cost tools
cost.role: Analyze billed spend with Cost Explorer; alert through Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection.
cost.boundary: Billing signals and API request throttles do not implement a hard team token budget.
details: Cost Explorer groups supported billing data by the required dimensions/tags.
Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection provide configured cost notifications.
Combine billing with application attribution; enforce hard admission limits in your own path.
cost.useWhen: You need billed-cost analysis, budget notifications, or unusual-spend investigation.

tracing.name: OpenTelemetry / X-Ray
tracing.role: Trace request stages, dependency latency, and errors with application instrumentation.
tracing.boundary: Instrument each relevant call and stream consumption; prefer current OpenTelemetry guidance.
details: Create correlated spans around each relevant SDK call and logical stage.
Measure streaming consumption as well as request initiation.
Use OpenTelemetry/ADOT and the configured exporter/backend to inspect failures and latency.
tracing.useWhen: A request spans model, retrieval, tool, and application dependencies.

cloudtrail.name: AWS CloudTrail
cloudtrail.role: Record supported AWS API activity and caller context for audit.
cloudtrail.boundary: Enable relevant data events; source API access alone does not describe returned retrieval evidence.
details: Record management activity and explicitly enable the required data-event coverage.
Inspect identity, action, resource, time, and result context.
Correlate API evidence with application records for the document, answer, or business action.
cloudtrail.useWhen: Investigations need supported AWS API activity and caller evidence.

invlog.name: Model invocation logging
invlog.role: Capture supported model request/response records in configured CloudWatch/S3 destinations.
invlog.boundary: Opt in deliberately: raw sensitive content can be captured before masking.
details: Opt in through the invocation-logging configuration and choose destinations/modalities.
Inspect operation, model, caller identity, payload references, and token counts.
Set access, encryption, retention, and delivery monitoring before capturing sensitive content.
invlog.useWhen: You need supported model request/response records for controlled diagnostics.

config.name: AWS Config
config.role: Record resource configurations/history and evaluate configured compliance rules.
config.boundary: Resource configuration checks differ from AppConfig deployments and framework audit evidence.
details: Record supported resource configuration items and changes.
Evaluate selected rules or conformance packs and investigate noncompliance.
Connect findings to an authorized remediation process where appropriate.
config.useWhen: Resource configuration history or rule-based configuration compliance is required.

qbusiness.name: Amazon Q Business
qbusiness.role: Packaged enterprise assistant with connected content and configured identity/access integration.
qbusiness.boundary: Closed to new customers; assess Amazon Quick and documented migration gaps.
details: Connect supported enterprise sources and synchronize content/access information.
Configure user identity and evaluate the returned content under real entitlements.
Assess current availability and migration requirements before extending the deployment.
qbusiness.useWhen: An existing eligible deployment needs a packaged enterprise assistant experience.

availability.text: Closed to new customers; check Amazon Quick and migration guidance.

quick.name: Amazon Quick
quick.role: Managed work assistant for connected data, analysis, workflows, and agentic actions.
quick.boundary: Assess connector, identity, authorization, and migration requirements for the actual workload.
details: Evaluate the supported connected-data, analysis, workflow, and assistant capabilities.
Configure identity, connector permissions, and authorized downstream actions.
Test access preservation and feature gaps for the actual migration/workflow.
quick.useWhen: A supported managed employee experience fits better than building the complete application.

qdeveloper.name: Amazon Q Developer
qdeveloper.role: Assist supported development, transformation, review, and repository workflows.
qdeveloper.boundary: An issue URL is not repository authorization; verify current interfaces and lifecycle guidance.
details: Distinguish transformation, code/security review, and issue implementation workflows.
Authorize the specific repository/integration rather than relying on an issue URL.
Review generated changes and tests; check interface availability and lifecycle notices.
qdeveloper.useWhen: A supported development, modernization, or repository workflow fits the task.

availability.text: Feature availability differs by integration; the Q Developer IDE plugin ends support on 30 April 2027.

sts.name: AWS STS
sts.role: Issue temporary AWS credentials for an authorized role session using supported trust mechanisms.
sts.boundary: A federation token must satisfy provider and role trust; resulting credentials remain subject to AWS authorization.
details: AssumeRole uses an authorized AWS principal; SAML and web identity use their matching federation APIs.
Configure the provider and role trust, including relevant identity/token conditions.
Use the returned access key, secret, session token, and expiry through an authorized AWS SDK call.
sts.useWhen: External automation, such as CI, must call AWS without stored long-lived access keys.

verified.name: Amazon Verified Permissions
verified.role: Evaluate fine-grained application access using Cedar policies and trusted principal/resource context.
verified.boundary: The application enforces ALLOW/DENY; a decision is not a login session or AWS credentials.
details: Define principal, action, resource, and context under a Cedar schema/policy store.
Evaluate trusted identity/resource facts against policies.
Enforce the decision in the backend before reading data or executing the business action.
verified.useWhen: An authenticated application needs fine-grained user/resource/action decisions.

accessanalyzer.name: IAM Access Analyzer
accessanalyzer.role: Validate IAM policies and analyze configured external, internal, or unused access.
accessanalyzer.boundary: Findings help review permissions; Access Analyzer is not the per-request authorizer.
details: Validate policy syntax and supported security checks.
Use the configured analyzer type for supported external, internal, or unused-access findings.
Review and fix the relevant policy; a finding does not enforce the application request.
accessanalyzer.useWhen: IAM policies or configured access relationships need review before or after deployment.

artifact.name: AWS Artifact
artifact.role: Retrieve AWS compliance reports, certifications, and agreements on demand.
artifact.boundary: AWS assurance evidence is different from continuous auditing of your workloads.
details: Retrieve available AWS assurance documents and applicable agreements on demand.
Check the report scope, reporting period, and relevant AWS services.
Combine AWS evidence with the customer controls you must operate and document.
artifact.useWhen: Auditors need AWS-provided compliance reports or agreements.

auditmanager.name: AWS Audit Manager
auditmanager.role: Collect configured evidence against selected framework controls for assessments and audit review.
auditmanager.boundary: Evidence is not certification; check existing-account/Region eligibility and supported data sources.
details: Select a framework and assessment scope, including the applicable accounts/services.
Collect supported automated evidence and add/review manual evidence as needed.
Organize the assessment report and retain reviewer decisions; evidence alone is not certification.
auditmanager.useWhen: An existing eligible assessment needs evidence mapped to framework controls.

availability.text: Maintenance mode restricts new setup; existing organization exceptions have specific scope.

inspector.name: Amazon Inspector
inspector.role: Continuously assess supported workloads for applicable vulnerabilities and unintended exposure.
inspector.boundary: Resource eligibility and scan coverage differ; review and remediate findings.
details: Enable the applicable scanning type for supported compute/container workloads.
Review resource/package context, severity, and remediation guidance in findings.
Prioritize fixes and verify scan coverage instead of assuming every resource is assessed.
inspector.useWhen: Supported workloads need vulnerability and exposure assessment.

securityhub.name: AWS Security Hub
securityhub.role: Centralize and prioritize supported findings; CSPM supplies posture checks and service integrations.
securityhub.boundary: A findings view is different from raw API logs or proof of compliance.
details: Enable the required accounts, Regions, service integrations, and posture capabilities.
Triage supported findings by severity, resource context, and workflow state.
Route response work and verify remediation with the originating controls.
securityhub.useWhen: Security teams need supported findings and posture signals in a central workflow.

zones.title: Model lifecycle

stages.title: Select & customize
stages.boundary: As-is or customize? Evaluate the unchanged baseline first.

stages.title: Where the model runs
stages.boundary: Both host; choose by the control you need.

stages.title: Release & rollback
stages.boundary: Approved ≠ deployed; retain a compatible rollback.

zones.notesSummary: Hosting, endpoint modes, customization, adapters, and safe releases

zones.title: Knowledge / data flow

stages.title: Source & prepare
stages.boundary: A catalogue describes data; ingestion builds search evidence.

stages.title: Preprocess / extract
stages.boundary: Preserve meaning and structure before chunking.

stages.title: Ingestion
stages.boundary: Document → parse → chunk → metadata → embed → index.

stages.title: Knowledge store
stages.boundary: Choose by search needs, relationships, consistency, and cost.

stages.title: Retrieval & debug
stages.boundary: Find the first broken stage before changing the model.

zones.notesSummary: Extraction APIs, chunking, retrieval filters, indexing, and freshness

zones.title: Runtime / inference flow

stages.title: Front door & streaming
stages.boundary: Match the transport to the client exchange.

stages.title: Prompt / context
stages.boundary: Management stores versions; optimization proposes revisions.

stages.title: Model inference
stages.boundary: Shared versus native request; evaluate sampling changes.

stages.title: Session state, bots & voice
stages.boundary: The model only sees state you pass.

stages.title: Cost levers
stages.boundary: Cache what repeats; route by measured difficulty.

stages.title: Capacity & Regions
stages.boundary: Reserve, spread, or stay on-demand within policy.

stages.title: Slow versus starved
stages.boundary: Response delivery and model capacity are different.

zones.notesSummary: Invocation APIs, capacity, caching, streaming, and application state

zones.title: Pillar · Orchestration
zones.flow: Who chooses the next step? State · retries · approvals

stages.title: Who drives the next step
stages.boundary: Known states, model-selected actions, or one bounded handler.

stages.title: Events & queues
stages.boundary: React, schedule, and buffer; retain workflow state separately.

stages.title: Your agent platform
stages.boundary: Code + identity + bounded tools.

stages.title: When things fail
stages.boundary: Retry ≠ re-plan ≠ circuit breaker; make side effects safe.

zones.notesSummary: AgentCore, MCP, Step Functions, Flows, events, and recovery

zones.title: Pillar · Security / governance

stages.title: Who is the caller?
stages.boundary: App users, workforce users, workloads, and agents.

stages.title: What may they call?
stages.boundary: AWS API permission and record entitlement are separate.

stages.title: Private path
stages.boundary: Configure connectivity and permission at their own boundaries.

stages.title: Data controls
stages.boundary: Keys, lake permissions, retention, HTTP protection, sensitive data.

stages.title: Content safety
stages.boundary: Filter content; authorize documents and tools separately.

zones.notesSummary: Access paths, protocols, private endpoints, redaction, and retention

zones.title: Pillar · Evaluation & observability
zones.flow: Quality before release + evidence from production

stages.title: Prove quality
stages.boundary: Held-out data + rubric + critical-cohort release gates.

stages.title: Watch production
stages.boundary: Choose evidence that answers the operational question.

stages.title: Security, compliance & audit
stages.boundary: AWS assurance and customer workload evidence have different owners.

zones.notesSummary: Evaluation metrics, regression gates, traces, logs, and audit evidence

zones.title: Packaged apps

stages.title: Packaged assistants
stages.boundary: Product workflow versus custom application ownership.

zones.notesSummary: Employee assistants, developer workflows, and service availability

examples.title: Documents with approval
examples.need: A known batch of reports needs extraction, analysis, and a human decision.
examples.boundary: Map iterates the reports; approval waits in the workflow. The final business write needs authorization and idempotency.

examples.title: A maintenance action
examples.need: An agent diagnoses a pump and proposes a work order.
examples.boundary: The maintenance API authorizes the exact plant/action and reconciles retries. Conversation memory is not the plant record.

examples.title: Fresh, governed knowledge
examples.need: New manuals must become searchable without indexing invalid or sensitive text.
examples.boundary: Compare retrieval before generation. A reranker cannot fix missing ingestion, and metadata scope must come from trusted identity.

examples.title: A voice assistant
examples.need: Users speak and receive incremental spoken replies.
examples.boundary: Choose a compatible streaming path at every hop and measure end-to-end latency; use WebSockets when bidirectional push is required.

examples.title: Promote a candidate safely
examples.need: A prompt/model change must pass quality checks and reach the intended route.
examples.boundary: Prompt-only changes may not need a model package. Verify the actual live version; sandbox shadow writes and retain a compatible rollback target.

sagemaker-flow.title: Example workflow
sagemaker-flow.code:
Prepare data → train/tune → evaluate
→ approve model package
→ create/update endpoint → verify live route
sagemaker-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

neo-flow.title: Example workflow
neo-flow.code:
Trained model + supported target
→ compilation job → compiled artifact
→ compatible edge/device runtime
neo-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

hybrid-flow.title: Example workflow
hybrid-flow.code:
On-premises requirement → evaluate Outposts
Mobile carrier edge → evaluate Wavelength
Check all data and service dependencies
hybrid-flow.note: Infrastructure location does not prove that every application dependency is local.

registry-flow.title: Example workflow
registry-flow.code:
Candidate artifact + evaluation evidence
→ model package version → approval
→ release pipeline → verified endpoint
registry-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

cicd-flow.title: Example workflow
cicd-flow.code:
Commit → build → held-out evaluation
→ business/schema assertions → release gate
→ deploy → verify actual route → monitor
cicd-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

datawrangler-flow.title: Example workflow
datawrangler-flow.code:
Raw dataset → Data Wrangler preparation
→ Processing script → versioned S3 output
→ training or evaluation pipeline
datawrangler-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

neptune-flow.title: Example workflow
neptune-flow.code:
Question → entity/relationship retrieval
→ supporting graph-linked evidence
→ grounded answer + source references
neptune-flow.note: Conceptual GraphRAG path; managed Knowledge Bases has its own graph-build and retrieval contract.

agentcore-flow.title: Example workflow
agentcore-flow.code:
Authenticated request → authorized agent
→ model/tool planning → scoped tool call
→ validated result → response + telemetry
agentcore-flow.note: Select Runtime/managed harness, Gateway, Identity, and memory components according to the workload.

agentidentity-flow.title: Example workflow
agentidentity-flow.code:
Inbound: trusted identity → agent access
Outbound: agent + scoped request
→ configured credential provider → target API
agentidentity-flow.note: Inbound authentication, outbound credential access, and target business authorization are separate checks.

multiagent-flow.title: Example workflow
multiagent-flow.code:
Request → supervisor/router
→ selected specialist + scoped context
→ validated handoff/result → final response
multiagent-flow.note: Define allowed tools, termination, and task-completion evaluation across all handoffs.

flows-flow.title: Example workflow
flows-flow.code:
Flow input → draft prompt → classifier
→ deterministic condition
→ polish / review branch → flow output
flows-flow.note: Pass the original draft as well as the classification to downstream nodes; handle malformed classifications.

cognito-flow.title: Example workflow
cognito-flow.code:
User → user pool / external IdP
→ ID token for client + access token for API
→ API validates token → application policy
cognito-flow.note: User-pool tokens are not AWS access keys. An identity pool adds an optional temporary-credential exchange.

idc-flow.title: Example workflow
idc-flow.code:
Employee → corporate IdP
→ SAML federation → Identity Center
→ assigned account/permission set
→ temporary role credentials → signed AWS API
idc-flow.note: SCIM provisions users/groups; SAML federates sign-in. A permission set does not define document ACLs.

vpce-flow.title: Example workflow
vpce-flow.code:
Workload → private DNS
→ bedrock-runtime endpoint ENI
→ endpoint + IAM policy checks
→ supported model API
vpce-flow.note: Configure network reachability and the correct service endpoint. A private endpoint does not grant IAM permission.

kms-flow.title: Example workflow
kms-flow.code:
Application role → authorized secret read
→ required KMS decrypt permission
→ use credential for intended target
→ redact logs + rotate as configured
kms-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

lakeformation-flow.title: Example workflow
lakeformation-flow.code:
Trusted query identity → integrated engine
→ Lake Formation grants/data filters
→ permitted table/column/row result
lakeformation-flow.note: Remove direct source paths that could bypass the integrated permission check.

waf-flow.title: Example workflow
waf-flow.code:
HTTP request → supported protected resource
→ web ACL rules / abuse controls
→ application authentication + authorization
waf-flow.note: Web-request filtering and model-content policies have different responsibilities.

macie-flow.title: Example workflow
macie-flow.code:
Eligible S3 objects → discovery/job
→ sensitive-data findings + coverage review
→ verified remediation/redaction workflow
macie-flow.note: A finding does not alter the object. Review skipped and unsupported objects.

evaluations-flow.title: Example workflow
evaluations-flow.code:
Versioned prompts + references + rubric
→ candidate/baseline outputs → evaluation job
→ report → critical-cohort thresholds
→ promote or halt
evaluations-flow.note: This is a release workflow, not a CreateEvaluationJob request. The input schema depends on the chosen evaluation type.

human-flow.title: Example workflow
human-flow.code:
Ground Truth: source data → labeling task
→ work team → training labels
A2I: selected prediction → human loop
→ reviewed result → application handling
human-flow.note: Existing-customer eligibility applies. Reviewed results do not automatically retrain the model.

clarify-flow.title: Example workflow
clarify-flow.code:
Before release: held-out data → bias analysis
→ report → configured release threshold
Production: captured data → baseline comparison
→ drift signal → task-quality investigation
clarify-flow.note: Existing-customer eligibility applies; analysis completion is not the pass/fail gate.

modelcard-flow.title: Example workflow
modelcard-flow.code:
Model/version → intended use + limitations
→ evaluation evidence + risks
→ documented release decision
→ governance/monitoring coverage review
modelcard-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

synthetics-flow.title: Example workflow
synthetics-flow.code:
Scheduled canary → sign-in/API journey
→ assert expected response/workflow
→ latency/failure evidence → alarm
synthetics-flow.note: A smoke check covers its configured journey; use representative datasets for broader quality evaluation.

cost-flow.title: Example workflow
cost-flow.code:
Billing data + supported allocation tags
→ Cost Explorer analysis
→ budget/anomaly notification
→ investigation + application admission policy
cost-flow.note: Billing alerts are not synchronous hard token-budget enforcement.

tracing-flow.title: Example workflow
tracing-flow.code:
request_id + deployed_version
└─ API span
   ├─ retrieval span
   ├─ model call + stream-consumption span
   └─ authorized tool span
tracing-flow.note: Conceptual span hierarchy; sanitize attributes and configure an OpenTelemetry exporter/backend.

config-flow.title: Example workflow
config-flow.code:
Resource change → configuration record
→ selected rule evaluation
→ compliant/noncompliant finding
→ authorized remediation + verification
config-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

qbusiness-flow.title: Example workflow
qbusiness-flow.code:
Employee sign-in → connected enterprise data
→ synchronized document ACLs
→ permitted retrieved answer
qbusiness-flow.note: For existing eligible deployments; assess availability and migration feature gaps.

quick-flow.title: Example workflow
quick-flow.code:
Employee identity → connected work data
→ authorized analysis / workflow / assistant
→ permitted answer or downstream action
quick-flow.note: Check supported connectors, entitlements, and action permissions for the actual product workflow.

qdeveloper-flow.title: Example workflow
qdeveloper-flow.code:
Authorized repository + task
→ supported transformation / review / change
→ inspect diff → run checks
→ normal review and release process
qdeveloper-flow.note: Conceptual development workflow; verify current integration availability and lifecycle guidance.

artifact-flow.title: Example workflow
artifact-flow.code:
Auditor request → AWS Artifact
→ select report + period + scope
→ retrieve available assurance document
→ combine with customer-control evidence
artifact-flow.note: Artifact supplies AWS assurance documents on demand; it does not continuously scan customer infrastructure.

auditmanager-flow.title: Example workflow
auditmanager-flow.code:
Selected framework + assessment scope
→ supported automated/manual evidence
→ reviewer assessment → audit report
auditmanager-flow.note: Check existing-account/Region eligibility. Evidence collection does not certify compliance.

inspector-flow.title: Example workflow
inspector-flow.code:
Supported workload + enabled scan type
→ vulnerability/exposure assessment
→ prioritized finding → remediation
→ verify fix and scan coverage
inspector-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

securityhub-flow.title: Example workflow
securityhub-flow.code:
Supported security services + posture checks
→ centralized findings + resource context
→ triage/prioritize → response workflow
→ verify remediation at source
securityhub-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

converse-request.title: Converse request
converse-request.note: Illustrative values. modelId is an SDK argument / HTTP path parameter. Optional serviceTier uses default (Standard), priority, flex, or reserved for compatible models; Reserved requires configured capacity.

converse-response.title: What to read from the response
converse-response.note: Token counts and text are illustrative; check stopReason as well as the returned content.

native-messages.title: Native Messages request body
native-messages.format: JSON · Anthropic Messages body for InvokeModel
native-messages.note: Serialize this as the InvokeModel body and choose a supported Anthropic modelId. Other model families use different payloads.

inference-config.title: Supported output controls
inference-config.note: Merge into a compatible Converse request. Select sampling settings by evaluation; output length cannot enlarge the context window.

routing-config.title: Versioned model configuration
routing-config.note: Example configuration content, not an AppConfig API request. Validate, deploy, retrieve, and enforce it in the application.

get-parameter.title: GetParameter
get-parameter.note: Use an existing parameter and scoped ssm:GetParameter permission; encrypted values also require the applicable KMS access.

get-source.title: Read a specific source version
get-source.note: Use an accessible versioned object. Carry its identity into derived chunk metadata; indexed access needs separate authorization.

quality-rules.title: Gate the approved dataset
quality-rules.note: Configure pipeline failure or quarantine based on results. Trim or separately test whitespace-only strings.

analyze-document.title: AnalyzeDocument
analyze-document.note: Use supported input and permissions. Inspect Blocks, relationships, and confidence; use an appropriate async API for longer documents.

transcribe-job.title: StartTranscriptionJob
transcribe-job.note: Use an accessible media object and output destination. Speaker labels do not establish business roles.

detect-pii.title: DetectPiiEntities
detect-pii.note: Synthetic text. Detection returns spans; your application must apply and verify redaction.

pii-result.title: How returned spans are used
pii-result.note: Illustrative result for the exact synthetic input above. Apply offsets to the same analyzed text.

detect-phi.title: DetectPHI
detect-phi.note: Synthetic clinical text. Verify supported entity types and offsets before applying redaction.

image-labels.title: DetectLabels
image-labels.note: Illustrative label count/threshold, not a universal preset. Check image support and S3 permissions.

retrieve-request.title: Retrieve authorized candidates
retrieve-request.format: JSON · Bedrock Agent Runtime SDK arguments
retrieve-request.note: Derive tenant-a from trusted backend identity. Require indexed metadata and supported filtering; this example uses vectorSearchConfiguration.

rag-request.title: RetrieveAndGenerate
rag-request.format: JSON · request body for a supported Knowledge Base
rag-request.note: Use the appropriate tenant scope and supported model. RetrieveAndGenerate does not support managed Knowledge Bases; select the API for the KB type.

titan-embedding.title: Titan Text Embeddings V2 body
titan-embedding.note: Use the compatible Titan V2 model and match corpus/query configuration. The returned embedding length follows the supported dimension choice.

knn-search.title: Vector candidate search
knn-search.note: The three-number vector is illustrative. Match the configured knn_vector field dimension/engine and add your supported trusted filter.

pgvector-query.title: Similarity with a tenant predicate
pgvector-query.code:
SELECT id, content
FROM chunks
WHERE tenant_id = $1
ORDER BY embedding <=> $2::vector
LIMIT 5;
pgvector-query.note: Bind trusted tenant scope and a compatible query vector. The cosine-distance operator requires pgvector; benchmark the selected index/filter behavior.

kendra-query.title: Query with an attribute constraint
kendra-query.note: For an existing eligible index with the custom field configured. Derive scope server-side; attribute filters do not replace required ACL/user-context integration.

rerank-request.title: Rerank existing candidates
rerank-request.note: Supply actual retrieved candidates and an eligible model ARN. Use returned relevance/index information to select context.

streaming-integration.title: Enable a supported streaming integration
streaming-integration.note: Fragment only: configure the supported integration URI/method and end-to-end streaming path. This is not an HTTP API setting.

graphql-contract.title: Application GraphQL schema
graphql-contract.note: Application-owned schema: configure resolvers and authorization. Enforce ownership of requestId at the backend.

prompt-version.title: Invoke an existing prompt version
prompt-version.note: The prompt must define question and its model/settings. With a prompt ARN, configure inference/system/tool fields in Prompt Management, not conflicting request fields.

promptopt-flow.title: Example workflow
promptopt-flow.code:
Baseline prompt + supported target model
→ optimization job → proposed revision
→ same held-out tasks → compare quality/cost
→ promote a version only if it passes
promptopt-flow.note: Conceptual sequence; configure each service and its permissions separately.

idempotency-write.title: Claim a new application action
idempotency-write.note: Illustrative table design. Handle conditional failure, tenant scope, external side effects, and reconciliation; the write alone is not exactly-once execution.

recognize-text.title: RecognizeText
recognize-text.format: JSON · Lex Runtime V2 SDK arguments
recognize-text.note: Use a deployed bot/alias with configured intents and fulfillment permissions.

synthesize-speech.title: SynthesizeSpeech
synthesize-speech.note: Example voice/engine selection; verify availability and language/engine compatibility in the chosen Region.

router-request.title: Invoke the supported prompt router
router-request.note: Use an existing supported router. A custom cascade instead makes application-controlled sequential calls.

cache-checkpoint.title: Mark a supported reusable prefix
cache-checkpoint.note: Place inside a compatible message. The real prefix must meet model-specific minimum/expiry rules; this placeholder is not a cacheable-length example.

answer-cache.title: Validate before reusing an answer
answer-cache.code:
key = tenant + entitlements + corpus_version
    + model_prompt_policy_version + request
hit = cache.lookup(key)
if hit and still_authorized(hit) and fresh(hit):
    return hit.answer
answer-cache.note: Conceptual key construction, not production hashing code. A semantic hit also needs task-tested equivalence; similarity alone is not authorization.

shared-cache.title: Choose the cache boundary
shared-cache.code:
Shared public reference → cacheable response
Private tenant answer → explicit cache policy
User entitlement changes → invalidate/revalidate
shared-cache.note: Conceptual examples, not a CloudFront distribution configuration.

provisioned-model.title: Invoke the reserved resource
provisioned-model.note: Use a supported ready provisioned resource. Calling the base model ID instead does not direct traffic to this reservation.

profile-model.title: Invoke the approved profile
profile-model.note: Approve the actual destination list and applicable IAM/SCP route. An application inference profile can add supported usage attribution.

tool-arguments.title: A tool call with bounded arguments
tool-arguments.note: Example arguments for an application-defined tool, not a complete MCP JSON-RPC envelope. Derive user/plant scope from trusted runtime context.

invoke-classic.title: InvokeAgent with trace enabled
invoke-classic.format: JSON · Bedrock Agent Runtime SDK arguments
invoke-classic.note: Existing eligible Classic deployment only. Consume the returned event stream; trace observations do not replace business API authorization.

state-machine.title: A deterministic approval branch
state-machine.note: The trusted prior step must obtain the approval decision. This branch alone does not implement authentication or a human callback wait.

tool-event.title: A scoped tool-handler input
tool-event.note: Application event, not an AWS API request. Authenticate and derive tenant/plant entitlements from a trusted context before executing the action.

s3-pattern.title: Match an S3 object-created event
s3-pattern.note: Enable S3 EventBridge delivery, then configure a supported target and its permissions. A matching rule does not perform the ingestion itself.

queue-message.title: SendMessage
queue-message.note: Standard-queue example. Configure consumers, retries, visibility, and deduplication/idempotency; limit concurrency/tokens in the worker.

iam-statement.title: Scope an AWS model permission
iam-statement.note: Permission statement only; place it in an applicable policy. Streaming needs its own action, and inference profiles need their additional profile/destination contract.

retention-contract.title: Keep the obligations separate
retention-contract.code:
Immutable retention/legal hold → Object Lock
Age-based transition/expiry → Lifecycle
Derived copies → their own retention/delete plan
retention-contract.note: Retention/legal holds can prevent eligible deletion; deleting a source does not automatically remove indexed or cached copies.

guardrail-call.title: ApplyGuardrail independently
guardrail-call.note: Configure policies first and inspect action/output. This assesses supported content; it does not invoke a model or grant tool permissions.

token-query.title: Inspect captured token trends
token-query.code:
fields @timestamp, input.inputTokenCount, output.outputTokenCount
| stats avg(input.inputTokenCount) as avgInput,
        avg(output.outputTokenCount) as avgOutput
  by bin(1h)
token-query.note: Run against enabled invocation logs with these fields. Metrics and billing answer different operational questions.

trail-event.title: What an API audit record tells you
trail-event.note: Illustrative subset, not a complete record. Verify event coverage/type; this does not contain the full answer or prove document-level access.

invocation-record.title: Invocation-log record fields
invocation-record.note: Logging is opt-in. Actual fields/payload delivery depend on the operation, modality, and configured destinations.

web-identity.title: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
web-identity.note: Role trust must accept the configured OIDC provider and relevant claims. A SAML assertion instead uses AssumeRoleWithSAML.

authorization-request.title: IsAuthorized
authorization-request.note: Use your Cedar schema, policies, and trusted entity/context facts. Enforce the returned ALLOW/DENY; this is not user sign-in.

validate-policy.title: ValidatePolicy
validate-policy.format: JSON · IAM Access Analyzer SDK arguments
validate-policy.note: Review returned findings and test effective access. Validation is not per-request authorization.

bda-invocation.title: InvokeDataAutomationAsync
bda-invocation.format: JSON · Bedrock Data Automation Runtime SDK arguments
bda-invocation.note: Use a configured project, supported file, profile ARN, and permissions. Inspect asynchronous status before consuming output; extraction does not create embeddings.

vector-query.title: QueryVectors
vector-query.note: Three values illustrate the shape; match the real index dimension/model. Derive filter scope from trusted identity. Filtering or returned metadata needs both QueryVectors and GetVectors permissions.

cognito-token.title: What the API validates
cognito-token.note: Decoded claims only, not a complete or usable signed JWT. Validate signature, trusted issuer, client/token type, expiry, and required scopes. This token is not an AWS access key.

oidc-trust.title: The role must also trust the workload
oidc-trust.note: GitHub Actions example. Configure the OIDC provider and the exact permitted audience/subject; environment-based subjects differ. Trust permits the exchange; role permission policies still govern AWS actions.

sagemaker-serverless.title: Serverless endpoint configuration with warm capacity
sagemaker-serverless.note: ModelName must reference a compatible model created first. CreateEndpoint deploys this configuration. Omit ProvisionedConcurrency for on-demand serverless; keeping it adds warm-capacity charges. Both use CPU, with no InstanceType/GPU selection.

qualifier.title: Architecture before services
qualifier.question: What are you trying to minimize?

options.then: Prefer managed capabilities when their controls fit.
Keep a compatible client/API boundary; change behind it.
Use supported features and integrations before custom code.

qualifier.foot: First meet latency, scale, residency, security, and availability requirements. Then compare what your team must operate, change, or build.

gap.title: Close a quality gap — which lever?
gap.question: What is actually missing?

options.then: Eligible continued pre-training on unlabelled data

gap.foot: Start with the unchanged model as a baseline, then prompt → RAG → justified customization. Tuning is not a source-refresh pipeline; quantization is a separate compression technique.

hosting.title: Where does the model run?
hosting.question: Which control matters?

options.then: Supported base, customized, or imported models
Serverless; no GPU, even with Provisioned Concurrency
Trace every dependency and data location

hosting.foot: Both Bedrock and SageMaker host models. The fork is the control you need. Open a card for capacity, GPU, and billing comparisons.

config.title: Release, configuration, or compliance?
config.question: What changes?

options.then: Register evidence; deploy and verify separately
Validate, roll out, monitor, roll back
Parameter tiers / throughput are separate choices

config.foot: Approved ≠ deployed. Retain a compatible rollback and evaluate the actual application route.

prepare.title: Prepare the right source
prepare.question: Which responsibility?
prepare.foot: A Data Catalog describes data; it is not the vector index. Source updates still need ingestion.

extract.title: Choose extraction from the output
extract.question: What is the input?

options.then: Text, forms, tables, queries, expense/ID APIs
Transcribe; distinguish speakers from recorded channels
General NLP; apply any required redaction

extract.foot: Readable is not always faithful: preserve tables, meaning, and source references before chunking.

ingest.title: Build searchable evidence
ingest.question: Which preparation decision?

options.then: Choose the supported KB and source contract
Use compatible embedding models and versions

ingest.foot: Ingestion: parse → chunk → metadata → embed → index. Retrieval and reranking happen for each query.

vector.title: Choose a store or retriever
vector.question: What does the workload need?

options.then: Evaluate index, ranking, and capacity options
Check filters, connectors, and measured latency
Check eligibility, ACL sync, and connectors

vector.foot: Benchmark recall, latency, filtering, synchronization, and total cost. There is no universal vector-count cutoff.

rag.title: Wrong RAG answer — find the first broken stage
rag.question: Is the right evidence in Retrieve results?

options.then: Source → extraction → sync → chunks → embeddings → trusted filters
Test supported hybrid search or decomposition
Fix metadata, sync, deletion, and user scope
Inspect prompt, model behavior, output cap, evaluation

rag.foot: A reranker cannot recover an absent candidate. Fix retrieval before attributing every failure to the model.

stream.title: How does the answer reach the client?
stream.question: Which exchange?

options.then: Supported REST API streaming integration + model events
WebSocket; manage connection and job state

stream.foot: For API Gateway, response streaming is REST-only. HTTP APIs do not provide that feature; check the whole transport path.

prompt.title: Store a prompt or improve it?
prompt.question: Which job?

options.then: Evaluate the proposed candidate before release

prompt.foot: Versioning and optimization do not themselves approve a production release.

params.title: Choose the API, then tune output
params.question: What needs attention?

options.then: Tune supported sampling on representative tasks
Inspect stopReason and the output-token limit
Select evidence or split/synthesize; parameters cannot enlarge it
Concise format, tested output cap, context pruning

params.foot: No universal temperature/top-p preset guarantees quality. Check model-specific fields and token limits.

session.title: State, fixed intents, or speech?
session.question: What does the application need?

options.then: Persist scoped records and enforce expiry

session.foot: These can compose. The model only receives the conversation state you include in the request.

cost.title: Cut repeated work or route by difficulty
cost.question: What repeats?

options.then: Exact/semantic application cache with versioned keys
Use a deliberate CDN cache policy
Supported managed routing, or a tested custom cascade
