cost.foot: Cache keys and hits must respect tenant permissions, source versions, model/prompt configuration, and deletion.

capacity.title: Choose capacity within the residency boundary
capacity.question: Traffic and processing location?

options.then: Compare reserved service tier and Provisioned Throughput
Supported geographic/global profile; approve every destination
Verify the regional model path and all dependencies
Supported batch job, separate from one async invocation

capacity.foot: Capacity, service tiers, routing profiles, and streaming are different choices. Reservations can incur idle/commitment charges.

latency.title: Slow response or insufficient throughput?
latency.question: Where is time or capacity lost?

options.then: Measure retrieval, model time-to-first-token, transport buffering
Check warm model and compute capacity separately
Pace work; review concurrency, tokens, quotas, capacity

latency.foot: Streaming improves incremental delivery; it does not by itself add model throughput.

driver.title: Who chooses the next step?
driver.question: Is the path known in advance?

options.then: Step Functions Standard; callbacks and eligible .sync jobs
Bound the agent loop, authority, and iterations

driver.foot: Express allows Wait states within its five-minute limit. External writes still need safe retry/idempotency behavior.

events.title: Route events or retain work?
events.question: What arrives?

options.then: Configure notifications for Lambda, SNS, or standard SQS
S3 EventBridge delivery + rule + supported target
Queue + paced consumers, visibility timeout, DLQ

events.foot: Direct S3 notifications do not target Step Functions or SQS FIFO. A delivered event is not proof that downstream work succeeded.

mcphost.title: Connect tools or host code?
mcphost.question: What do you already have?

options.then: Evaluate Gateway adapters before building a server
Configure supported trust and credential flows
Choose a suitable runtime and own its operations

mcphost.foot: Runtime hosts; Gateway connects; MCP standardizes tool interaction. The target still authorizes each action.

resilience.title: Recover from the actual failure
resilience.question: Which failure?

options.then: Bound retries with backoff, deadlines, idempotency
Bound iterations, tool authority, tokens, time
Halt promotion or roll back a compatible approved version

resilience.foot: Retry, agent re-planning, circuit breaking, and rollback solve different failures.

identity.title: Choose the caller path
identity.question: Who or what needs access?

options.then: Corporate IdP → Identity Center → assigned role/permission set
Trusted OIDC assertion → STS → temporary role credentials
IAM role → SDK temporary credentials → AWS API
Check inbound caller trust and outbound tool credentials

identity.foot: Cognito, workforce SSO, and OIDC can compose. Choose by principal, target, trust, and authorization needs.

authorize.title: Authentication is not permission
authorize.question: Which access question?

options.when: May this principal assume the role?
May this AWS session call the API?
May this user read the record / act?
Who could access, or what is unused?

authorize.foot: A JWT is not an AWS access key. Temporary AWS credentials normally sign AWS requests with SigV4. SCPs and permission boundaries limit permissions; they do not grant them.

private.title: Private connectivity and enforcement
private.question: Which requirement?

options.when: Private route to a supported service
options.then: Correct endpoint, DNS, and network rules
Applicable IAM, resource, endpoint, and organizational policies

private.foot: The pipe and the permission are separate. An endpoint policy does not grant access or automatically close every other path.

protect.title: Choose the data control
protect.question: What must be protected?

options.then: Object Lock / Lifecycle; include derived copies
WAF rules and selected managed protections

protect.foot: Data discovery, retention, network protection, and authorization address different obligations.

safety.title: Content safety or action authority?
safety.question: What must be controlled?

options.then: Selected Guardrails policies; handle block/mask results

safety.foot: Guardrails does not authorize access. Treat retrieved/tool content as untrusted and validate proposed actions outside the model.

reliable.title: Prove quality before release
reliable.question: What must the output satisfy?

options.then: Validate structure; use authorized deterministic tools
Calibrated fallback or supported human review

reliable.foot: Compare baseline/candidate on the same important cohorts. A citation, model confidence, or completed evaluation job alone does not prove correctness.

observe.title: Quality or runtime health?
observe.question: What is the symptom?
observe.foot: Operational health and answer quality need different evidence. Instrument the application, retrieval, model, and tools together.

audit.title: Select the evidence, not just a security label
audit.question: What do you need to know?
audit.foot: Artifact is not a continuous workload auditor. Configure collection, review findings, and resolve issues; see the shared-responsibility guide.

product.title: Buy an experience or build an application?
product.question: Which ownership fits?

options.then: Check connectors, identity, permissions, and plan
